package_info.package_versions: Pre-patch versions prior to July 2019 update (CVE-2019-2234)
package_info.why_malicious: The camera apps contained vulnerabilities that allowed unprivileged, rogue applications to bypass permission checks and control the camera and microphone, enabling unauthorized photo, video, and audio capture, as well as exfiltration of sensitive media and location data.

execution_context.file_location: malicious app code (client-side, e.g., Weather app)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a persistent connection to a remote C&C server, receives commands, and abuses camera intents to take photos, record videos, and extract GPS metadata, then uploads this data to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app performs camera and microphone operations without user interaction or explicit permissions, and exfiltrates sensitive data to a remote server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps require explicit camera/microphone permissions and user consent for such actions; this app bypasses those requirements.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate remote management or parental control apps may use similar logic, but only with explicit user consent and proper permissions.
key_indicators: Persistent C&C connection from a benign-appearing app
Triggering camera/microphone actions without user interaction
Exfiltration of media and metadata to external server

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon receiving C&C command or sensor event)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses stored photos, parses EXIF metadata for GPS location, and sends this location data to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app accesses and exfiltrates sensitive location data embedded in user photos without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps with storage access do not parse and exfiltrate GPS metadata from photos without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Photo management apps may read EXIF data for sorting or mapping, but not for exfiltration.
key_indicators: Automated parsing of EXIF GPS data

execution_context.trigger: runtime (during voice call, detected via proximity sensor)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a voice call is detected via the proximity sensor, the code records video and audio from both sides of the conversation and uploads it to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Recording both video and audio during a call without user consent is highly invasive and violates privacy expectations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps cannot record calls or video without explicit permissions and user awareness.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Call recording apps exist, but require explicit permissions and user consent.
key_indicators: Use of proximity sensor to trigger recording
Simultaneous video and audio capture during calls

attack_chain.action: Malicious app is installed and establishes a persistent connection to the attacker's C&C server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote attacker can issue commands to the device.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues commands to take photos, record videos, or wait for a call to record audio/video.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device captures sensitive media without user knowledge.

attack_chain.action: Malicious app accesses stored photos and parses EXIF GPS metadata.
Captured media and metadata are uploaded to the attacker's C&C server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive user data (photos, videos, audio, location).

behavioral_signatures: Unusual camera or microphone activation by apps without camera/mic permissions
Persistent outbound connections to remote servers from non-network-centric apps
Automated access to and parsing of EXIF GPS metadata in user photos
Media capture actions triggered by proximity sensor or during voice calls
file_indicators: Unexpected new photos or videos in camera roll
App accessing camera/media storage without user interaction
App package names mimicking benign utilities (e.g., weather apps) but requesting storage/network permissions
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C&C infrastructure
Frequent uploads of media files to external servers
Unusual network activity from apps not expected to use the network
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that access camera or microphone functionality without holding the appropriate permissions, especially if they also establish persistent network connections or access media storage in the background. Flag apps that parse EXIF GPS data and transmit it externally. Use behavioral analysis to detect camera/mic activation triggered by non-standard events (e.g., proximity sensor, call state) and correlate with network exfiltration of media files.
